stories.headline: Fifth Antalya Diplomacy Forum hosts 23 heads of state, Erdoğan holds intensive bilateral meetings
stories.summary: Turkey hosted the 5th Antalya Diplomacy Forum (April 17-19) under the theme 'Mapping Tomorrow, Managing Uncertainties,' with Erdoğan conducting bilateral meetings with leaders from Syria, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Libya, Slovenia, Comoros, DRC, Burundi, Iraqi Kurdistan (Barzani), and Pakistan, among others. Erdoğan also hosted Russia's Federation Council Chair Matviyenko and OSCE Secretary General Sinirlioğlu separately at Dolmabahçe, and spoke at the 152nd Inter-Parliamentary Union General Assembly in Istanbul.

stories.headline: İmamoğlu trial continues as police raids target additional CHP-run municipalities
stories.summary: The 23rd hearing in the Istanbul criminal case against detained Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu proceeded, with bodyguards and officials making their defense. Concurrently, police arrested Ataşehir Mayor Onursal Adıgüzel in a dawn raid and detained multiple CHP officials, adding to an existing wave of operations against opposition-run municipalities. From prison, İmamoğlu published a widely-circulated article ('Çare Millettir') calling for elections and condemning the crackdown, while CHP leader Özel returned from Spain to lead a rally in Ataşehir.

stories.headline: US Ambassador Barrack's 'merciful monarchy' remarks at ADF trigger political storm in Turkey
stories.summary: US Ambassador to Turkey Tom Barrack stated at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum that 'the only thing that ever worked in the Middle East was strong leadership regimes — either merciful monarchies or benevolent authoritarian regimes,' triggering widespread condemnation from opposition figures. Detained İmamoğlu called the remarks 'unacceptable,' CHP criticized AKP's silence as weakness, while Barrack also separately said US-Turkey would 'soon' resolve the S-400 sanctions issue. Separately, AKP was criticized for not responding to Barrack's comments.

stories.headline: Turkey mediates US-Iran ceasefire, hosts regional foreign ministers meeting at ADF margins
stories.summary: Turkey actively worked to extend the US-Iran ceasefire and continue negotiations, with Erdoğan stating Ankara was 'hopeful' despite stumbling blocks. Foreign ministers of Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt met on the sidelines of ADF to discuss the situation. Turkey called for both sides to be 'constructive,' while Fidan said he believed the ceasefire would hold. Erdoğan also called for the Strait of Hormuz to remain open to commercial shipping.

stories.headline: Two school shootings in southeastern Turkey kill nine, wound dozens within two days
stories.summary: A 14-year-old student killed eight fellow students and a teacher at a middle school in Kahramanmaraş on April 15, Turkey's second school shooting in two days following a separate attack in Şanlıurfa that left 16 injured. Erdoğan, Bahçeli, and Emine Erdoğan all made public statements; Erdoğan warned against politicizing the tragedy while promising a full investigation. CHP called for the Kahramanmaraş provincial education director's resignation, and the Education Ministry announced prayers at school openings on April 20.

stories.headline: TCMB April rate decision approaching; market survey raises year-end inflation forecast to 27.5%
stories.summary: Turkey's Central Bank is scheduled to announce its April 22 policy rate decision, with economists overwhelmingly expecting rates to remain at 37%. The Bank's April market participants survey revised year-end inflation expectations upward from 25.38% to 27.53%. TCMB's total reserves rose $9.27 billion to $170.9 billion in the week ending April 10. Governor Karahan is also scheduled to present to parliament's Planning and Budget Commission on May 5.
